verdict.headline: The Fed raises rates for the first time since 2023, with only the path after it unsettled
verdict.label: FOMC announces 2:00 p.m. ET with a quarter point to 3.75%-4.00% priced near 93%, the first increase since July 2023. Markets price roughly 41.2 bp of total 2026 tightening against eleven banks at 50 and BofA, Deutsche Bank and RBC at 75. WTI -1.29% to $104.46 and Brent -1.02% to $107.64 on an unexpected US crude build, the first decline in a week. Ten-year at 5.008% after a 5.041% high, its highest since July 2007. S&P futures +0.2%, Nasdaq-100 +0.4%. August retail sales at 8:30 a.m.
verdict.rationale_short:
The Federal Open Market Committee announces at 2:00 p.m. Eastern, with futures pricing a quarter-point increase to 3.75%-4.00% at roughly 93% — the first rise since July 2023. With the rate itself settled, the Summary of Economic Projections carries the meeting, and the disagreement it lands in is measurable rather than rhetorical. Market pricing implies about 41.2 basis points of total 2026 tightening, today's move included, which is barely one more increase. Eleven banks including Barclays, Citigroup, Nomura, UBS and Wells Fargo forecast 50 basis points for the year; Bank of America, Deutsche Bank and RBC forecast 75; Goldman Sachs expects none after today. An 85% majority of economists, 86 of 101, told Reuters the Fed would move today, and 37 of 70 expect at least one further increase by end-March, with the majority view no longer calling for lower rates in 2027 at all. The median dot is the committee's own entry into that spread.

The second fact this morning is that crude is falling for the first time in a week. WTI for October is down 1.29% to $104.46 and Brent for November 1.02% to $107.64 on an unexpected increase in US crude inventories. The Saudi East-West pipeline has been shut since the September 10 drone attack with no restart timeline, so the supply loss that drove the month's roughly 22% gain has not been resolved — it has been offset by barrels arriving elsewhere. That distinction matters for the decision: crude is the input that carried the ten-year to 5.008%, its highest since July 19, 2007, and its first close at 5% since 2007. A hawkish median therefore arrives at a market that has just begun pricing relief on the pressure that made the path a question in the first place.

Equities are taking the oil pullback rather than the yield. S&P 500 futures are up 0.2%, Nasdaq-100 futures 0.4% and Dow futures 0.1%, with the ten-year still above 5% — the reverse of the sequence that produced Tuesday's decline in all three indices. Gold recovered about 1% to $4,338 after touching a six-week low near $4,263 on Tuesday, when a firmer dollar and higher real yields pushed it down; a metal bidding into a hike priced at 93% is positioning for the projections, not for the rate. August retail sales print at 8:30 a.m., six hours ahead of the decision and the only growth reading between the inflation data that forced this hike and the hike itself, after July sales fell 0.6% against expectations of a 0.1% rise.

The evidence does cut both ways on how firmly any of this should be read. The VIX closed at 17.10, lower on a session the S&P 500 fell, which is a market reducing exposure ahead of a decision rather than hedging against it — not the profile of one that expects the projections to reset the path. Against that, the October-September VIX futures spread has widened to 2.2%, with the September contract expiring on Fed day, so what hedging demand exists sits after the meeting rather than into it.

The levels that would change the picture: a ten-year back under 4.90% after 2:00 p.m. would say the committee validated the roughly 41 basis points the market prices for 2026, and a hold above Tuesday's 5.041% high would say it sided with the 50-to-75 basis point camp. A WTI settle back under $100 would take the energy input out of the long end on supply arithmetic alone, with no diplomacy behind it.
verdict.lede_short: The Fed raises rates today for the first time since 2023, a quarter point to 3.75%-4.00% priced near 93% — so the projections, not the rate, carry the meeting. Markets price about 41 basis points of total 2026 tightening while eleven banks forecast 50 and three forecast 75, and the median dot is the committee's entry into that spread. Crude fell 1.3% to $104.46 on a US inventory build, so a hawkish median lands on a market already pricing relief.

Market pricing implies roughly 41.2 basis points of total 2026 tightening against Bank of America's 75, with eleven banks including Barclays, Citigroup, Nomura, UBS and Wells Fargo at 50 — the median dot is the committee's own entry into a spread running from Goldman's zero-more to three hikes in total

At $75,961 as of 6:01 a.m. ET, 1.3% above the $75,000 area that has held since August and down about 1% from Tuesday's close, after the Senate blocked the Clarity Act 49-50. Holding the level through a delivered hike would say both the legislative outcome and the rate were discounted in advance.

trade_setups.asset: The median 2026 dot against market pricing
trade_setups.thesis: The rate is settled at roughly 93% priced, so the disagreement the meeting resolves is about the path, and it is measurable. Market pricing implies about 41.2 basis points of total 2026 tightening including today's move — barely one more increase. Eleven banks forecast 50 for the year, Bank of America, Deutsche Bank and RBC forecast 75, Goldman Sachs expects none after today, and 37 of 70 economists in the Reuters panel expect at least one further increase by end-March. What is forming is a test of which side of that spread the committee publishes. The counter-evidence is that the VIX fell into the decision, which is not the profile of a market expecting the projections to reset anything.
trade_setups.entry: 4.90% and 5.041% on the ten-year are the levels that define it; 5.008% is this morning's reference print, and roughly 41 basis points is what the market currently charges for the year.
trade_setups.invalidation: A ten-year back under 4.90% after 2:00 p.m. would say the committee validated market pricing; a hold above Tuesday's 5.041% high would say it sided with the 50-to-75 basis point camp.
trade_setups.horizon: 2:00 p.m. Wednesday through the sessions that follow

trade_setups.asset: Crude between the inventory build and the pipeline
trade_setups.thesis: The first down day in a week came from a US crude stock build rather than from a restart or a meeting — no Hormuz talks have been rescheduled since Oman's postponement, and the Saudi East-West line is still shut with no timeline. What is forming is a question about whether a weekly inventory number can offset a structural outage that has added roughly 22% to the barrel this month. Refined-product costs reach the CPI basket with a four-to-six-week lag, so the level that holds here lands in the data the committee reads in November rather than next month.
trade_setups.entry: $100 below and $105 above are the levels that define it; $104.46 is this morning's reference print against Tuesday's $106.12 settle. The pipeline restart announcement remains the observable.
trade_setups.invalidation: A WTI settle back under $100 would say the premium is deflating on supply arithmetic alone; a return above $105 would say the build was a weekly artifact against a structural outage.
trade_setups.horizon: Two to six weeks, through the October CPI reporting period

trade_setups.thesis: Bitcoin at $75,961 sits 1.3% above the area that has held since August, after the Senate blocked the Clarity Act 49-50 on Tuesday and removed market-structure legislation from 2026. What is forming is a test of whether the asset trades on its own regulatory news or as a duration proxy: a delivered hike and a hawkish dot plot are a rates event, not a crypto one, so the reaction separates the two explanations. Against that, the legislative outcome was arithmetically visible in advance, and the decline after the vote was about the size of the decline into it.
trade_setups.entry: $75,000 is the level that defines it; $75,961 is this morning's reference print, with the exchange and issuer equities the faster-moving read.
trade_setups.invalidation: Holding $75,000 through a delivered hike would say both the legislative outcome and the rate were discounted in advance; losing it on the decision would say the asset is still trading as a duration proxy.
